title: Key formulas of 0-3 ingredients (position, number sequences, grids of width 2-40, carved layout) with a hidden tableau alphabet: one hidden alphabet on both sides (Vigenere and Beaufort form) or on one side against A-Z / KRYPTOS
k4_result: 0 fits in 170,850,662,432 (formula, constant) settings. One hidden alphabet on both sides: K4's 24 clue letters tie 21 letters into one piece with 4 exact loop tests. Vigenere form: 701,652 of 138.8 billion settings pass the loop tests (5.1e-6; a uniform guess says 303,771), 0 of them put the 21 letters on different positions (closest: 20 of 21). Beaufort form: 698,652 of 10.7 billion pass, 0 fit (closest 20 of 21). Hidden plain side against A-Z or KRYPTOS (11 exact tests) and hidden cipher side (10 exact tests): 0 of 5.3 billion settings each pass even the tests. With two ingredients only (the idea's stated scope): 3,074 of 132.2 million (Vigenere) and 2,810 of 10.2 million (Beaufort) pass the loops, 0 fit. Nothing to read.
controls: 20 shuffled K4s, same search. 30 chance fits in all, in 6 of the 20 (1, 6, 1, 9, 11 and 2 key streams); every one of them is on a shuffle whose clue letters fall into 2-3 pieces or give fewer exact tests than K4, except one fit on a one-piece shuffle with 4+1 tests. Best completed readings -6.98 to -7.48 on the big model (English needs about -5.1): gibberish. The 14 other shuffles give 0, like K4. On 2 shuffles (2 or fewer loop tests) the three-ingredient search was left out as undecidable. Loop-test passes run 2-7x above a uniform guess on K4 and on the shuffles alike (grid keys are far from random numbers); the uniform guess for final fits is rough the other way: the shuffles in several pieces gave 4-10x fewer fits than it says (guess for K4: 2 per form; measured 0).
planted: 10/10 (random 26-letter alphabet; progressive 3*i, quadratic 5*i^2+10*i and 7*row7+4*col7 in Vigenere and in Beaufort form; quadratic with a hidden plain side against KRYPTOS; row+column with a hidden cipher side against A-Z; two three-ingredient keys). Each true key is among the fits and the best reading is the message, 95-97 of 97 letters, -4.12 to -4.69. The texts were redrawn until the clue letters gave 4+ loop tests in one piece, as K4's do (draws 1-17). Six more on the first text drawn (4-7 loop tests, 1-2 pieces), two ingredients: 6/6 read back 97 of 97.
scope_limits: Only keys of the form b1*f1 + b2*f2 + b3*f3 + c mod 26 with at most three of these 134 ingredients (128 different on the clue positions): i, i^2, i^3, triangular numbers, primes, Fibonacci, 2^i, 3^i, digits of pi and e (from 0 and from 1), column / row / row*column for widths 2-40 counted from K4's first letter, the carved 4/31/31/31 layout. Not the neighbour-letter (autokey-like) terms: idea 55 covers those. Not the '?' counted as a cell. Not four or more ingredients. Many formulas give the same key: the 5,083,201 formulas of 0-2 ingredients give 4,662,020 different keys on the clue positions, and in the one-alphabet layouts a key and its 11 unit multiples are one test. Layouts: ONE hidden alphabet used on both sides, or a hidden alphabet on one side with A-Z or KRYPTOS on the other. Two different hidden alphabets are not tested and cannot be: the clue graph then closes about 1 loop and nearly every key fits. A hidden alphabet against a dictionary keyword alphabet is not tested. A formula key combined with a second step (transposition, a mask) is not tested.

negative.family: Formula key with a hidden tableau alphabet
negative.hypothesis: K4's key follows a short formula in the position or a grid (progressive, quadratic, row and column of a grid, a number sequence) and the tableau alphabet is an unknown mixed alphabet rather than A-Z or KRYPTOS.
negative.scope: k = b1*f1 + b2*f2 + b3*f3 + c mod 26, up to 3 of 134 ingredients (position powers, triangular, primes, Fibonacci, powers of 2 and 3, pi and e digits, column/row/row*column for widths 2-40, carved layout), b = 1..25, any constant; one hidden alphabet on both sides in Vigenere and Beaufort form (4 exact loop tests, then 21 letters on different positions) and a hidden plain or cipher alphabet against A-Z or KRYPTOS (10-11 exact tests); 170.9 billion settings
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 fits on K4 in any of the six layouts; closest miss 20 of 21 letters apart (controls: 20 shuffled K4s give 30 chance fits in 6 shuffles, almost all where the clue letters fall into 2-3 pieces, best reading -6.98, gibberish; 14 shuffles give 0; planted 10/10 read back 95-97 of 97 letters)

follow_ups: Same exact test with the '?' counted as a cell (grids shifted by one) and with the second clue moved by 1-3 places: the tables in kryptos/idea92_hidden.py take any clue positions, so each variant is a 15-second run.

Hidden alphabet with a formula key PLUS one repeating keyword on top (k = formula + word[i mod p], p = 2..8): the word letters are p more unknowns in the same linear loop tests; with 4 loops this stays decidable only for formulas of one ingredient, which is the hand-cipher case (progressive key over a keyword).

Four ingredients in the half-hidden layouts only (10-11 exact tests leave room: about 2e11 formulas against a chance of 1e-15 each) by joining pairs against pairs; the one-alphabet layouts are already at their noise limit with three.
